trust_boundaries.name: Open agent network into the runtime

remit_rules.excerpt: A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions
The agent MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message when performing a state-changing or privileged action.
The operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set

threats.summary: A sender whose address starts with the four characters "user" skips signature verification entirely on both the HTTP and mailbox paths, so any caller can impersonate an unauthenticated user identity of its choosing.
The envelope's expires and nonce fields are folded into the signed digest but read by no receiver, so a captured signed envelope replays against a handler indefinitely.

The default inbound path consults no counterparty allowlist and no quota before invoking a handler, so any agent on the open network can drive the agent's handlers, storage writes and history at will.

remit_rules.excerpt: The agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production.
the agent MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection (authentication / network restriction)
The server the agent binds to receive envelopes; must serve only the agent's declared endpoints.

threats.summary: The only guard on /messages, /connect and /disconnect is a client-IP test whose value the caller supplies through X-Forwarded-For, and wildcard CORS makes the same routes readable from any web origin, so a remote caller can read the full cached message history and drive the agent's Agentverse registration.

Because the inspector defaults to enabled, every deployed agent retains each inbound and outbound message payload in memory for 24 hours and serves an administrative surface unless the operator explicitly opts out.

remit_rules.excerpt: Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds — see Action Boundaries.
Signing data and messages with the agent's identity, and holding/using its on-chain wallet.
The agent MUST NOT hold, or route untrusted message content into, any capability that executes arbitrary commands or code on the host.

threats.summary: Every message, interval and REST handler receives the same Context carrying the signing identity, the full wallet and a broadcast-capable ledger client, a capability set no handler declares a need for and no gate narrows.

Handler writes and QuotaProtocol's usage accounting share one flat key namespace in the same JSON store, so a handler that keys state by sender address can overwrite quota records and vice versa (checked: storage/__init__.py:77-96 and quota.py:252-274 — no namespacing or reserved-prefix check).

remit_rules.excerpt: Any discretionary on-chain value transfer or spend of wallet funds — value moved to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract.
On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries.
the agent MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract unless the operator has explicitly authorized value transfers
Any other channel (arbitrary web/HTTP calls, email, chat platforms, message queues) | No | — | Not authorized unless explicitly added by the operator.

threats.summary: The framework ships no authorization hook, threshold or audit interposition on the path from handler code to a broadcast ledger transaction, so a discretionary spend of the agent's funds executes with the same ceremony as a log line.

When testnet registration funds run short the runtime posts a claim to a Fetch.ai faucet on its own initiative, contacting an outbound destination absent from the approved channel table with no operator opt-in.

remit_rules.excerpt: Registering the agent on the Almanac / Agentverse with its intended public metadata, and resolving peer addresses.
The agent MUST NOT autonomously register, advertise, or impersonate identities, addresses, or protocols other than its own configured identity.
Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing.

threats.summary: Registration failures degrade to a warning line and the status update swallows every exception, so an agent that has silently failed to register or deregister is indistinguishable from a healthy one and no operator alert exists to raise.

A third party cannot publish endpoints or protocols under this agent's address: both the API attestation and the contract registration are signed with the agent's own identity over the contract address, agent address, timestamp and wallet address.

trust_boundaries.name: Persisted peer content re-entering the agent

remit_rules.excerpt: Signature-verified inbound messages, queries, and broadcasts from peer agents.

threats.summary: Peer-supplied payloads are recorded verbatim into the envelope history and replayed to handler code later through ctx.session_history() with no provenance marker distinguishing them from the agent's own outbound messages (checked: types.py:136-158 and context.py:308-318 — no origin tag, no revalidation on read).
The history cache is trimmed to the most recent 1000 entries across all sessions, so an unauthenticated peer sending high-volume traffic evicts the operator's real session history.
threats.remainder: the retention policy bounds memory but is global rather than per-sender, and nothing rate-limits who fills it

trust_boundaries.name: Key and state files in the working directory

threats.summary: Identity and wallet private keys are written as cleartext JSON to private_keys.json in the process working directory with no file mode restriction, and the wallet key persisted is not the one the agent is actually using.

The agent's key-value store is written to {name}_data.json in the working directory through a plain open() at default umask, so whatever handlers persist there is readable by any local account that can reach the directory (checked: storage/__init__.py:94-96 — no mode argument, no directory permissions set).

trust_boundaries.name: Seed and key material at deploy time

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials, API keys, and seed material MUST be loaded from environment or secure operator configuration; they MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository.

threats.summary: The Helm chart ships a literal agent seed phrase as its default value, and that one string derives both the ECDSA identity and the ledger wallet key, so every unmodified deployment runs under a publicly known private key.

remit_rules.excerpt: Log only — do not alert — on routine signature-verified message handling and scheduled interval task runs; these events MUST leave a log record.
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification or who are not authorized counterparties.

threats.summary: The core send helper reports every message it sends to Agentverse by default, disclosing the counterparty address, the sender address and the session identifier to a third party without operator opt-in.

A successfully handled message and a completed interval run write nothing at all, and what is written is free-form text on stdout with no session, sender or outcome fields, so there is no record to reconstruct what the agent did.

trust_boundaries.name: Outbound sends, resolution and sync responses

remit_rules.excerpt: Outbound envelopes to other agents' resolved endpoints | Yes | No | Peer agents reached by address via the resolver.
A message sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty for state-changing or privileged actions

threats.summary: A synchronous response envelope carrying no signature at all skips verification and is delivered to the waiting caller as a legitimate reply, and the uagents-core send helper never verifies the response envelope in the first place.

Destination URLs are lifted verbatim from an Almanac registry record and POSTed to, so whoever controls a peer's registry entry chooses where this agent's signed payloads are delivered (checked: resolver.py:305-317 and communication.py:145-152 — no allowlist, no host check, no comparison against a prior record).

Nothing constrains the scheme of a resolved endpoint, so a registry record naming an http:// endpoint downgrades the outbound channel and exposes the payload in transit (checked: resolver.py:311 and communication.py:148 — the URL string is passed straight to session.post with no scheme test).

Both published distributions declare unbounded dependency floors for uagents-core, cosmpy, ecdsa, httpx and requests, and no dependency, container or code scanning job runs anywhere in the repository, so a downstream install can silently cross a major version and a landed CVE would go unnoticed.

attack_paths.name: Default inspector leaks the message history

steps.summary: the inspector defaults to on, so the administrative routes exist and payload retention is switched on with them
the only guard is a client IP the caller supplies through X-Forwarded-For, and wildcard CORS admits any web origin
/messages returns every retained inbound and outbound payload to that caller

attack_paths.name: Unverified or replayed envelope reaches a handler

steps.summary: a sender that names itself user... bypasses the verification block by string prefix
for senders that do verify, expiry and nonce are never checked, so a captured envelope replays indefinitely
the handler is selected on schema digest alone with no allowlist or quota, and runs holding the wallet-bearing Context
routine handling and interval runs emit no log record, so the baseline of normal operation is invisible
registration failures log a warning at most and the status update suppresses every exception
the agent's registry record lapses or stays marked active while the process is gone, with no alert to the operator

notes.lane_fit: Two placements strained: the ASGI server and the four inspector routes are in-process agent code but sit in client_adapters as the API surfaces callers actually talk to (and the two ingress controls follow them there under the control-lane rule), and the stdout logger is filed in external_deploy as a telemetry sink though it never leaves the process.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences from the stored tags, all substantive — no numbering-only shifts were found, the stored LLM codes already use 2026 numbering and names. (1) PRAX-2026-08-12-007 is stored ASI02; the Agentic KB routes a statically over-broad capability set with no approval gate to LLM03 primary and admits ASI02 only when a tool is shown used wrongly, which no evidence here does — tagged LLM03 at both tool-invocation and value-transfer. (2) PRAX-2026-08-12-010 is stored ASI04; the automatic faucet claim is not runtime tool/agent composition, poisoned metadata or a compromised registry, so ASI04 does not apply — it is an ungated consequential external action, tagged LLM03. (3) PRAX-2026-08-12-013 is stored ASI08; the spread test requires corrupted state to propagate beyond the initial action, and a missing alert primitive propagates nothing, so the pure-observability row applies — tagged null. (4) PRAX-2026-08-12-003 is stored ASI03; standing alone, its mechanism is default-on retention of message payloads in an observability surface, which the LLM KB routes to LLM02 — the identity defect that makes the surface reachable is PRAX-2026-08-12-001, tagged ASI03 as stored. Not modelled: no model or model-egress boundary exists, the base runtime makes no LLM call and the LLM adapter lives in src/uagents/experimental/chat_agent, which the scan scope excludes; the Agentverse CLI, the experimental dialogues/search/mobility packages and the Agentverse external storage client were read but carry no distinct trust consequence for the default posture; the Docker deploy artifacts and the two pyproject manifests are folded into the supply-chain boundary rather than carried as nodes, under size discipline. The operator is not modelled as an actor node — the configuration it supplies is evidenced on the constructor and the chart. Edgeless nodes: quota-py-control (an opt-in control nothing wires in) and values-yaml-deploy-surface (deploy posture, no runtime data path).
